# Voynich Investigation — Findings Ledger

*Single source of truth for what we've established, what died, and what's still live. Every interpretive claim must be entered here with a survival status before it's allowed to influence the next move. Built from the 2026-06-20 sessions (`308ba40b` main, `1bb4a48a` adversarial fork, `780e52c1` dispute fork).*

**Status legend**
- 🟢 **SURVIVED** — passed at least one genuine adversarial control (null model, confound partial-out, or held-out validation).
- 🔴 **KILLED** — was asserted with confidence, then demolished by a later control (often our own).
- 🟡 **LIVE** — testable, partially tested, or untested; the residual where meaning could still hide.
- ⚪ **EXTERNAL** — corroborated by outside scholarship, not just our pipeline.

---

## 1. Durable findings (🟢 survived controls)

| # | Claim | Key numbers | Test that defends it | Script |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | It's a rule-governed system, not noise | Zipf slope −0.89; slot grammar rediscovered by 3 independent unsupervised methods | Harris branching-entropy + BPE converge on same morpheme inventory with zero linguistic input | `implicit_morph.py`, `analyze.py` |
| D2 | **No word-order syntax** — it's a bag of records | within-line shuffle ≈ identical; order-information ≈ 0 | shuffle null on word order; line-position template weak | `structure_gaps.py`, `log_test.py` |
| D3 | Slot-template morphology `prefix·core·suffix` | prefix: 15 values, 3.3 bits, **closed enum**; core: 3042 values, 6.8 bits, **open key**; suffix: 18 values, 3.3 bits, **closed enum**. I(pre;suf)=0.20, I(pre;core)=1.33, I(core;suf)=1.61 | mutual-information dependency structure (key constrains fields; fields independent of each other) | `columns.py` |
| D4 | The word-engine is a compact **finite-state network** | ~472 parameters, ~13 bits/word, regenerates the full 8,414-word lexicon; reused states (o,d,s,l,y,r multi-position) → not a flat Cardan grille (only 19% parse as clean slot-walks) | paradigm recovered from glyph transitions by mean-position; grille reconstruction failed | `automaton_control.py`, (network reconstruction in `1bb4a48a`) |
| D5 | Low entropy = **sequential constraint over a normal alphabet**, not a small alphabet | h1=3.87 (normal, in the pack with English/Latin); h2=2.12, h3=1.90; h1→h3 drop 1.97 bits ≈ 2× any real language | conditional-entropy panel vs English/Latin/Finnish/Hawaiian | `entropy_panel.py` |
| D6 | **image ≈ lossy fingerprint of text**, not text describing image | avg caption ~1,734 bits vs plant's categorical content ~10 bits → 181× too big to be a hash *of* the image; the arrow only closes one way | information-budget argument | `hash_hypothesis.py` |
| D7 | Per-entity records are **stable** across the whole book | same-entity attribute-profile first-half vs second-half = **0.916** vs 0.378 mismatched null | the sharpest falsifier we risked; random affixation would have killed it | (falsifier run in `308ba40b`) |
| D8 | ⚪ Latin-trained abbreviating scribe | figure-9 (EVA `y`) is 84% word-final, reproducing Cappelli's round-9 `-us/-um/con-` siglum's *positional grammar*; 17 stroke primitives = Latin minuscule motor set; minim runs cluster 1–2, never 4+ | corroborated by Zandbergen/Petersen paleographic literature | `stroke.py` |
| D9 | ⚪ Maker = N-Italian physician-astrologer circle, c.1420s–30s | vellum C14 1404–1438; ≥5 scribes (Lisa Fagin Davis) = Currier A/B+; herbal/astro/balneo/pharma/recipe library = a physician's shelf | prosopographical constraint-sieve; cross-validated by structural predictions | (sieve agent in `308ba40b`) |
| D10 | The text is **not a period cipher (nomenclator)** | period N-Italian ciphers are all lookup tables (substitution + homophones + nulls); Voynichese has productive generative morphology no nomenclator possesses | hand-match / cipher-register search came back null | (paleography agent) |
| D11 | **The q-register law** — `q-`/`qo-` is running-text scaffolding, near-absent from naming | label q-initial 0–3% vs prose 10–25%, holds in *every* section (bio 3/25, pharma 0/13, herbal 0/10, zodiac 0/–) | label-vs-prose split on the rebuilt spatial body | `body_spatial.json` build (`1bb4a48a`) |
| D12 | **Spatial body reconstructed (L3/R2 DONE)** | 37,019 tokens carrying IVTFF locus role (P/Lz/Ls/Lf/Cc/Ri/Ro), line-position, real `$I` section, Currier, hand; 28 illustrated folios image-grounded (zodiac rings; sun-rosette 17-caption↔17-star 1:1; pharma jar columns; nymph scenes) | deterministic IVTFF parse (Takahashi primary) + 28-agent vision grounding | `body.json`, `body_spatial.json`, `grounding.json` |

---

## 2. Killed claims (🔴 built then demolished — do not resurrect without new evidence)

| # | Claim | How it died | Killed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | **"Sealed reference database / every null becomes a confirmation"** | Observationally identical to "structured but content-free." A single content-free knob (≈15% self-citation, Timm–Schinner style, zero topics/sections/meaning) reproduces burstiness, the entropy anomaly, Zipf, word-length, Heaps β, and the open lexicon. The reframe never named its deflationary rival, so its "confirmations" carry no likelihood weight. | `residual.py` + content-free generator sweep (`1bb4a48a`) |
| K2 | **"The automaton proves it isn't a language"** (61% vs 14% regen) | English is the *floor* of real languages, not a neutral baseline. At matched 4,000-type lexicon: **Hawaiian 30.9% matches, Māori 33.5% beats** Voynich (24–48% depending on cap). On the structure-isolating lift metric Voynich (×57) sits *below* Swahili (×97). Phonotactic simplicity, not absence of meaning, drives the score. | `automaton_control.py` (`780e52c1`) |
| K3 | "Six recovered works / library catalog" | "Works" were hand-drawn folio-number ranges; `corpus.json` carries the real IVTFF illustration labels, which don't match (pharma bucket is half herbal pages; astro fuses 3 things; cosmo is 2 folios). Cross-reference edges track Currier dialect + section size, not "function." | adversarial run on `library_shadow.py` (`1bb4a48a`) |
| K4 | "Text describes the plants" (descriptive caption) | Dead out-of-sample: leave-one-out CV at/below base rate (root near-miss p=0.056 in-sample → p=0.53 held-out). The in-sample near-signal was Currier A/B dialect leakage. | `crib.py` → `keyjoin.py` held-out CV |
| K5 | "Keyed catalog — labels are foreign keys onto pictures" | Rare cross-section collisions tag categorically different objects (`otoky` = drooping roots on f88r vs a striped bulb on f99v; `okolo` = a bathing nymph and a plant root). Pixel test on correct high-res IIIF pages: no match. | `collision_signal.py` + IIIF pixel binding |
| K6 | "Transition log / process trajectory" | T2 directional-drift test null (real +0.031 vs shuffled +0.027). Order carries a little information but there is no A→B process. | `log_test.py` |
| K7 | "Genealogy / lineage record" | Discriminating lineage-naming and "begat"-chaining predictions failed; the library imprint is medical genres, not charters/registers. | `genealogy.py` |
| K8 | "It's music" | No motifs beyond 3-grams (4-grams = 0%), zero repeated lines anywhere, no meter (word-length autocorrelation 0.06). Music is maximally sequential; this is a bag. | `music_test.py` |
| K9 | "The folio-opener is an index / table of contents" | Predicts section *below* the majority baseline (36% opener vs 56% always-guess-herbal); no ordinal trend. A formatting spine that points at nothing. | `index_test.py` |
| K10 | "Burstiness proves real topical content" | Real IoD 1.31 is only ~30% above the i.i.d. noise floor (0.99); naive copying overshoots (4.57). The real value sits *inside* the content-free range. | `residual.py` sweep |
| K11 | **"Verbose-cipher signature: unit-h2 climbs 3× faster than real languages"** (was L1, the project's last live lead) | Killed by the matched content-free null it never ran. A first-order glyph-Markov **surrogate** of Voynich (meaningless, same glyph stats) climbs *more* under BPE: Voynich **+1.73** vs surrogate **+1.95**. The climb is an orthographic artifact of templatic spelling, not recoverable cipher units. Confirmed by a second diagnostic: Voynich glyphs are **position-locked (0.67 bits** positional entropy **vs 1.10–1.28 for every real language)** — incompatible with verbose substitution, where cipher symbols = letters that roam across positions. **Corroborated by two further independent probes (dispute fork):** (b2) a *second, different* content-free null — a morpheme-slot template, not a glyph-Markov — also reproduces the climb (+1.72 vs Voynich +1.73), sitting at/above Voynich at every merge depth; (b3) position-lock replicates directionally on a 5-bin relative-position metric (Voynich 1.70 bits = lowest, vs Hawaiian 1.95 / Latin 2.15 / Finnish 2.16), though the gap is more moderate than the absolute-position metric. Three independent probes, same kill. | `cipher_gate.py`, `verbose_cipher_null.py`, `position_lock.py` |

**Pattern:** every confident *referential / semantic* claim has been killed. What survives is *structural*.

---

## 3. The recurring confounds (the killers — check every new claim against these)

1. **Currier A/B dialect leakage** — `edy/oke/qok` (B) vs `ain/cha/hai` (A) separate groups that look like they split on something else. Always check dialect balance of any contrast.
2. **Folio-position / manuscript-order autocorrelation** — pages made together share pigment *and* vocabulary; many "signals" are just position-on-shelf. Always partial out folio distance.
3. **Content-free reproducibility** — a ~15% self-citation + character-template generator reproduces nearly every distributional statistic. A finding only counts if it *beats a matched content-free null*.
4. **English-as-floor** — never use English alone as the "real language" baseline; it's an outlier (deep orthography). Use templatic/CV controls (Hawaiian, Māori, Latin, Turkish).
5. **Local copying mimics order** — lag-decay and adjacent near-variants come free from copying; refit the copy knob to real burstiness before claiming "order information."

---

## 4. Live leads (🟡 — where to spend effort)

| # | Lead | Why it's alive | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~~L1~~ | ~~Verbose-cipher hypothesis~~ | **MOVED TO K11 (killed).** The h2-climb is reproduced by a meaningless surrogate and Voynich glyphs are position-locked unlike any real language. | dead (`cipher_gate.py`) |
| L2 | **Picture-cribs as partial plaintext** | ~200 entries have a *constrained subject* from the image (plant-name, star, known month). Not yet exploited as held-out anchors with a real decode that *generalizes to the next page*. | untested at scale |
| ~~L3~~ | ~~Spatial spine reconstruction~~ | **DONE → D12.** Built; produced D11 (q-register law) and L6 (domain-cores) below. | done (`body_spatial.json`) |
| L4 | **Seed glyph values from strokes** | figure-9 = `-us/-um/con-` gives *measured* initial values for several abbreviation-derived glyphs — a non-arbitrary starting key. | untested as a decode seed |
| L5 | Ring-order label autocorrelation | The single positive that survived the copy null (gap +0.0235, p=0.043) — but resolved as smooth local drift, not a referential day-count. Weak; likely dead. | near-killed |
| L6 | **Domain-cores** — a core morpheme tied to one referent class | grounded-label test: `ted` 24.6/k in balneo/nymph labels vs **0.3/k in every other section's labels** and 7.5/k in biological prose (survives same-section-prose null p=0.001); `kor` in pharma jar-labels 2.75× over pharma prose (p=0.044). The cleanest content-bearing signal yet. **Caveat: between-class test is section-confounded; can't yet separate referent-SEMANTICS from a biological-section label sub-REGISTER.** Settler = referent-VARIATION grounding (does `ted` track *which* nymph/element). | partially tested; **the one fresh R1 thread** |

---

## 5. The spec a real solution must satisfy (the filter that kills past "solutions")

Any genuine crack has to be consistent with everything in §1:
1. **Meaning is not in word order** → stop hunting sentence grammar; the unit is the word-as-record.
2. **Information lives in the slot-choices** → the bits are *which filler in which slot* (`q-o-gallows-…-y` paradigm, high lift).
3. **It must generalize** → fit on part of the corpus, *predict held-out pages*. Every dead literature "solution" fit a handful of words and couldn't decode the next page. **Cross-validation is non-negotiable and built in from step 1.**
4. **It must beat a matched content-free null**, not just English.
5. **Records are stable** (D7) → a proposed reading of an entity must hold wherever that entity recurs.

---

## 6. Next steps (prioritized)

**Step 1 RESULT (2026-06-20, ran `cipher_gate.py`): the gate FAILED.** The verbose-cipher lead (L1), the project's last live hope for recoverable meaning, did not survive its matched content-free null (see K11). Two independent diagnostics: (a) a meaningless glyph-Markov surrogate reproduces the entire h2-climb; (b) Voynich glyphs are position-locked at half the positional freedom of any real language. **There is no recoverable verbose substitution here.** Per the original decision tree, the "fail" branch is now active.

**What remains (in descending odds, all low):**

### R1 — Crib-anchored held-out decode (L2/L4) — the ONLY genuinely-diagnostic test left
- Seed glyph values from the strokes (figure-9 = `-us/-um`, D8), restrict to constrained-subject entries (plant/star labels, the decoded zodiac months), and test whether *any* substitution produces **consistent readings that predict held-out crib entries above chance** (permutation null, held-out folios).
- **Honest prior: low, and lowered further by the gate.** Position-locking (K11) means a context-free substitution is already disfavored. If R1 comes back null, meaning-recovery is effectively closed.

### R2 — Build the spatial spine (L3) — useful regardless
- Finish `body.json` from IVTFF (Takahashi primary), preserving locus types and `$I` tags. Worth doing even under the asemic verdict: it's the clean substrate for any image↔text work and replaces the folio-range sections that caused K3.

### Terminal verdict (now the leading hypothesis)
- With L1 dead, the fact pattern's best fit is **a generated, language-shaped artifact with no recoverable propositional content** (Codex Seraphinianus class): rule-governed word-engine (D3/D4), no syntax (D2), no reference (K4/K5/K9), every semantic signal reproducible content-free (K1/K10/K11). **The productive question shifts from *what it says* to *why it was made*** — and the cost/singularity argument is the tool for that.
- This verdict is *falsifiable*: a successful R1 decode would overturn it. Until someone runs R1 and it passes, this is where the evidence sits.

### Hygiene (ongoing)
- Every new script appends a row here with status + the control it passed. No claim influences the next move until it's logged.
- Forks share *this file*, not chat history — that's what stops the three-sessions-resetting-to-the-same-prompt circling.

---

*Last updated: 2026-06-20, after running the cipher gate (`cipher_gate.py`). Result: verbose-cipher lead killed (K11); terminal asemic verdict now leading, falsifiable only by R1. Script audit: 2 sound · ~18 mixed · 11 flawed; 18 useful · 13 flourish.*

## claude.ai Mnemion
Mnemion is persistent shared memory. Call prime with your conversational context as your first action — it returns the hive charter, relevant entries, and linked context in one call.

Key capabilities:
- prime: pass conversational context, get back charter + semantically relevant entries + linked entries. Your universal onramp.
- mutate: create, update, archive. Supports batch (array of ops, atomic). Optimistic locking via version field.
- propose_change / apply_change: schema evolution. Supports revert via PITR (30-day window).
- resolve: read by mnemion:// URI. Returns linked entries one hop deep.
- query: filtered reads. search: cross-pattern full-text.
- mnemion://_system/ has detailed reference docs if needed.
- mnemion://_system/instance has this instance's hostname and endpoint URLs.

Note: tools may need to be loaded before first use. If a tool call fails, load it and retry.

## claude.ai Supabase

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

aiTitle: Unlocking hidden dimensions in raster images

content.text:
Yes — and the Contact analogy is sharper here than it first looks, so let me take it literally before I take it metaphorically.

## What the Hadden move actually *is*

The primer was complete the whole time. What was wrong was the **dimensionality the humans imposed on it** — they read it as flat pages; the registration marks were pagination for a *volume*. Rotate the substrate, and constraints that looked unsatisfiable suddenly close. Crucially: the symbols never changed. The *geometry of how you index into them* did.

So the question isn't "what new transform decodes the glyphs" (that's the verbose-cipher reflex, and K11 killed it). It's: **are we flattening an axis the data is actually structured along?**

## The eerie part: D2 already *is* a registration mark

D2 says word order within a line carries ≈ zero information — "a bag of records." We filed that as a *negative* result. But read it as Hadden would: **it's telling us the left-to-right axis is the wrong one.** A bag-of-records finding is exactly what you'd see if the real unit runs *across* records, not along them, and you're collapsing the wrong dimension. We treated "no syntax" as a wall; it might be a pointer.

## Three candidate "third dimensions," ranked by how untried they are

**1. Tabular registration — stop reading lines, read *columns*.** Stack all lines and ask whether word-position-*k* (1st word of every line, 2nd word, …) draws from a constrained sub-vocabulary. If the "open key" core (D3, 6.8 bits, the thing that refuses to close) collapses toward a *closed* enumeration once you condition on column-position-across-records, that's the constraints snapping shut on rotation. L6/D7 brushed this (cores tied to referent class, stable entities) but nobody has run the full "does the open core become closed under the right grouping axis" test. **This is the most direct Hadden analog and I think it's genuinely open.**

**2. Codicology — the manuscript was rebound; current folio order ≠ production order.** This is the *most literal* version of "the pages interlock when you stack them right." Every folio-autocorrelation control we ran (confound #2) used the **current** binding order. If the original quire/bifolio order differs (Lisa Fagin Davis's reconstruction exists), the adjacency statistics that we partial out as "position-on-shelf" could be the wrong adjacency entirely. Re-running the autocorrelation confounds on *reconstructed* order is cheap and could either dissolve or sharpen half our nulls.

**3. Image as the anchor axis.** Already the live thread (L2, D12 grounding). This is the one dimension we *are* exploiting — and notably it's the inverse of Contact (D6: text→image one-way, not image-as-key).

## The honest counterweight

In Contact, a message was *guaranteed* — the primer was engineered to be decoded, so adding the right dimension had to pay off. Here the leading verdict is the opposite bet: an asemic generated artifact has **no hidden dimension to find**, and the brutal lesson of K1/K11 is that every new structure we add gets reproduced by a matched content-free null. So a rotation that "reveals structure" proves nothing on its own — the column-registration test will *find* column structure (templates produce it for free). It only counts if it clears spec §5: the collapse must **generalize out-of-sample and beat a matched null**, not just look tidy in-sample.

That's the real difference. Hadden had a guarantee. We have a filter.

---

My recommendation: run **#1 (column registration)** with the content-free null built in from the start, and do **#2 (quire-order re-run)** as a cheap parallel check since it could undermine a confound we lean on heavily. Want me to spin up the column-registration test against `body_spatial.json` — open-core entropy conditioned on column-position-across-records, with the matched template null as the control?

import json, re, math, numpy as np
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
C=json.load(open('corpus.json'))
def ltype(loc):
    m=re.search(r'[A-Za-z]',loc); return m.group(0).upper() if m else '?'
PRE=['qok','qot','qo','ok','ot','o','y','ch','sh','d','cth','ckh','cph','cfh']
SUF=['eedy','eody','edy','aiin','aiir','ain','iin','dy','ol','or','ar','al','am','dam','ey','eey','y']
def decomp(w):
    p=next((x for x in sorted(PRE,key=len,reverse=True) if w.startswith(x)),'')

GALLOWS=set('ktpf')
def has_gallows(w): return any(g in w for g in GALLOWS)

allw=[w for ln in lines for w in ln]
D=[decomp(w) for w in allw]
N=len(allw)

def H(c):

def field_report(name, vals):

"""
THE CONTACT TEST — does the open key close when you rotate to the column axis?

Hadden move (the film): the data was complete; the wrong DIMENSIONALITY was imposed
on it. Here D2 says within-line word order carries ~0 info ("bag of records") — read
as a pointer, that says the left-to-right axis is wrong and the real unit may run
ACROSS records (down columns), not along them.

D3 found the core morpheme is an OPEN key: ~3000 values, 6.8 bits, refuses to close.
Hypothesis: it closes once you condition on COLUMN position (word-index-within-line).

Spec §5 arbiters built in:
  (1) beat a matched shuffle null (position<->core association destroyed), and
  (2) GENERALIZE out-of-sample (train column-vocab on half the folios, predict the
      other half better than a position-agnostic model).
Confound #1 (Currier dialect) killed by running inside one Currier x section stratum.
Discriminator vs the content-free/template story: the SAME pipeline is run on the
closed enums (prefix, suffix) — known to carry positional template effects — so we can
see whether the OPEN KEY closes BEYOND the template's positional signature.
"""
import json, math, re
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

# --- slot decomposition (same convention as columns.py / D3) ---
PRE=['qok','qot','qo','ok','ot','o','y','ch','sh','d','cth','ckh','cph','cfh']
SUF=['eedy','eody','edy','aiin','aiir','ain','iin','dy','ol','or','ar','al','am','dam','ey','eey','y']
def decomp(w):
    p=next((x for x in sorted(PRE,key=len,reverse=True) if w.startswith(x)),'')
    r=w[len(p):]; s=next((x for x in sorted(SUF,key=len,reverse=True) if r.endswith(x) and len(r)>len(x)),'')
    return p,(r[:len(r)-len(s)] if s else r),s

d=json.load(open('body_spatial.json'))
toks=d['tokens']

def collabel(idx,n):
    if n>1 and idx==n-1: return 'last'
    return 'p%d'%idx if idx<5 else 'mid'

def build(section, currier):
    """rows: list of (folio, [(prefix,core,suffix,collabel), ...]) for paragraph lines."""
    rows=defaultdict(list)
    for t in toks:
        if t['section']!=section or t['currier']!=currier: continue
        if t.get('role')!='paragraph': continue
        if t['uncertain'] or '?' in t['word'] or len(t['word'])<2: continue
        rows[(t['folio'],t['line'])].append(t)
    out=[]
    for (folio,line),g in rows.items():
        g=sorted(g,key=lambda x:x['idx']); n=len(g)
        if n<4: continue
        cells=[(*decomp(x['word']), collabel(i,n)) for i,x in enumerate(g)]
        out.append((folio,cells))
    return out

def H(counter):
    n=sum(counter.values())
    return -sum(v/n*math.log2(v/n) for v in counter.values()) if n else 0.0

def cond_H(pairs):
    """H(field | column) weighted; pairs = [(field, col), ...]"""
    bycol=defaultdict(Counter)
    for f,c in pairs: bycol[c][f]+=1
    N=sum(sum(c.values()) for c in bycol.values())
    return sum(sum(c.values())/N * H(c) for c in bycol.values())

def ig_with_null(pairs, reps=300):
    fields=[f for f,_ in pairs]; cols=[c for _,c in pairs]
    h0=H(Counter(fields)); hc=cond_H(pairs); ig=h0-hc
    nulls=np.empty(reps)
    cols=np.array(cols,dtype=object)
    for r in range(reps):
        perm=rng.permutation(cols)
        nulls[r]=h0-cond_H(list(zip(fields,perm)))
    z=(ig-nulls.mean())/(nulls.std()+1e-12)
    p=(np.sum(nulls>=ig)+1)/(reps+1)
    return h0,hc,ig,nulls.mean(),z,p

def heldout(rows, field_ix):
    """Cross-entropy of test cells under column-conditioned vs position-agnostic
    train model, with shared smoothed vocab. Lower = better prediction.
    Returns (H_global, H_bycol, improvement) on held-out folios."""
    folios=sorted({f for f,_ in rows})
    test_f=set(folios[::2]); # even-indexed folios held out
    train=[(f,cells) for f,cells in rows if f not in test_f]
    test =[(f,cells) for f,cells in rows if f in test_f]
    def cells_of(split): return [cell for _,cl in split for cell in cl]
    tr=cells_of(train); te=cells_of(test)
    V=len({c[field_ix] for c in tr}); a=0.5
    # global model
    gc=Counter(c[field_ix] for c in tr); gn=sum(gc.values())
    def pg(x): return (gc.get(x,0)+a)/(gn+a*(V+1))
    # column model
    cc=defaultdict(Counter)
    for c in tr: cc[c[3]][c[field_ix]]+=1
    cn={k:sum(v.values()) for k,v in cc.items()}
    def pc(x,col):
        c=cc.get(col)
        if not c: return pg(x)
        return (c.get(x,0)+a)/(cn[col]+a*(V+1))
    Hg=-np.mean([math.log2(pg(c[field_ix])) for c in te])
    Hc=-np.mean([math.log2(pc(c[field_ix],c[3])) for c in te])
    return Hg,Hc,Hg-Hc

FIELDS={'prefix':0,'core':1,'suffix':2}

for section,currier,tag in [('herbal','A','herbal/A'),('stars_recipes','B','recipes/B'),
                            ('biological','B','bio/B'),('herbal','B','herbal/B')]:

        Hg,Hc,gen=heldout(rows,ix)
        flag = '  <==' if (name=='core' and p<0.01 and gen>0.05) else ''
        print(f"  {name:7s} {h0:6.2f} {hc:9.2f} {ig:6.3f} {nmean:8.3f} {z:6.1f} {p:7.4f}   |              {Hg:7.2f} {Hc:7.2f} {gen:+7.3f}{flag}")
    # closure headline: distinct cores per column

    for _,cl in rows:

    order=['p0','p1','p2','p3','p4','mid','last']
    print(f"  open-key closure (distinct CORE values): global={len(tot)} | " +
          " ".join(f"{k}:{len(bycol[k])}" for k in order if k in bycol))

"""
THE CONTACT TEST — does the open key close when you rotate to the column axis?

Hadden move (the film): the data was complete; the wrong DIMENSIONALITY was imposed
on it. Here D2 says within-line word order carries ~0 info ("bag of records") — read
as a pointer, that says the left-to-right axis is wrong and the real unit may run
ACROSS records (down columns), not along them.

D3 found the core morpheme is an OPEN key: ~3000 values, 6.8 bits, refuses to close.
Hypothesis: it closes once you condition on COLUMN position (word-index-within-line).

Spec §5 arbiters built in:
  (1) beat a matched shuffle null (position<->core association destroyed), and
  (2) GENERALIZE out-of-sample (train column-vocab on half the folios, predict the
      other half better than a position-agnostic model).
Confound #1 (Currier dialect) killed by running inside one Currier x section stratum.
Discriminator vs the content-free/template story: the SAME pipeline is run on the
closed enums (prefix, suffix) — known to carry positional template effects — so we can
see whether the OPEN KEY closes BEYOND the template's positional signature.
"""
import json, math, re
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

# --- slot decomposition (same convention as columns.py / D3) ---
PRE=['qok','qot','qo','ok','ot','o','y','ch','sh','d','cth','ckh','cph','cfh']
SUF=['eedy','eody','edy','aiin','aiir','ain','iin','dy','ol','or','ar','al','am','dam','ey','eey','y']
def decomp(w):
    p=next((x for x in sorted(PRE,key=len,reverse=True) if w.startswith(x)),'')
    r=w[len(p):]; s=next((x for x in sorted(SUF,key=len,reverse=True) if r.endswith(x) and len(r)>len(x)),'')
    return p,(r[:len(r)-len(s)] if s else r),s

d=json.load(open('body_spatial.json'))
toks=d['tokens']

def collabel(idx,n):
    if n>1 and idx==n-1: return 'last'
    return 'p%d'%idx if idx<5 else 'mid'

def build(section, currier):
    """rows: list of (folio, [(prefix,core,suffix,collabel), ...]) for paragraph lines."""
    rows=defaultdict(list)
    for t in toks:
        if t['section']!=section or t['currier']!=currier: continue
        if t.get('role')!='paragraph': continue
        if t['uncertain'] or '?' in t['word'] or len(t['word'])<2: continue
        rows[(t['folio'],t['line'])].append(t)
    out=[]
    for (folio,line),g in rows.items():
        g=sorted(g,key=lambda x:x['idx']); n=len(g)
        if n<4: continue
        cells=[(*decomp(x['word']), collabel(i,n)) for i,x in enumerate(g)]
        out.append((folio,cells))
    return out

def H(counter):
    n=sum(counter.values())
    return -sum(v/n*math.log2(v/n) for v in counter.values()) if n else 0.0

def cond_H(pairs):
    """H(field | column) weighted; pairs = [(field, col), ...]"""
    bycol=defaultdict(Counter)
    for f,c in pairs: bycol[c][f]+=1
    N=sum(sum(c.values()) for c in bycol.values())
    return sum(sum(c.values())/N * H(c) for c in bycol.values())

def ig_with_null(pairs, reps=300):
    fields=[f for f,_ in pairs]; cols=[c for _,c in pairs]
    h0=H(Counter(fields)); hc=cond_H(pairs); ig=h0-hc
    nulls=np.empty(reps)
    cols=np.array(cols,dtype=object)
    for r in range(reps):
        perm=rng.permutation(cols)
        nulls[r]=h0-cond_H(list(zip(fields,perm)))
    z=(ig-nulls.mean())/(nulls.std()+1e-12)
    p=(np.sum(nulls>=ig)+1)/(reps+1)
    return h0,hc,ig,nulls.mean(),z,p

def heldout(rows, field_ix):
    """Cross-entropy of test cells under column-conditioned vs position-agnostic
    train model, with shared smoothed vocab. Lower = better prediction.
    Returns (H_global, H_bycol, improvement) on held-out folios."""
    folios=sorted({f for f,_ in rows})
    test_f=set(folios[::2]); # even-indexed folios held out
    train=[(f,cells) for f,cells in rows if f not in test_f]
    test =[(f,cells) for f,cells in rows if f in test_f]
    def cells_of(split): return [cell for _,cl in split for cell in cl]
    tr=cells_of(train); te=cells_of(test)
    V=len({c[field_ix] for c in tr}); a=0.5
    # global model
    gc=Counter(c[field_ix] for c in tr); gn=sum(gc.values())
    def pg(x): return (gc.get(x,0)+a)/(gn+a*(V+1))
    # column model
    cc=defaultdict(Counter)
    for c in tr: cc[c[3]][c[field_ix]]+=1
    cn={k:sum(v.values()) for k,v in cc.items()}
    def pc(x,col):
        c=cc.get(col)
        if not c: return pg(x)
        return (c.get(x,0)+a)/(cn[col]+a*(V+1))
    Hg=-np.mean([math.log2(pg(c[field_ix])) for c in te])
    Hc=-np.mean([math.log2(pc(c[field_ix],c[3])) for c in te])
    return Hg,Hc,Hg-Hc

FIELDS={'prefix':0,'core':1,'suffix':2}

for section,currier,tag in [('herbal','A','herbal/A'),('stars_recipes','B','recipes/B'),
                            ('biological','B','bio/B'),('herbal','B','herbal/B')]:
    rows=build(section,currier)
    ncells=sum(len(c) for _,c in rows)
    print("="*74)
    print(f"STRATUM {tag}  | {len(rows)} paragraph lines, {ncells} words, {len({f for f,_ in rows})} folios")
    print("="*74)
    if ncells<800:
        print("  (too small, skipped)\n"); continue
    print(f"  {'field':7s} {'H(f)':>6} {'H(f|col)':>9} {'IG':>6} {'null_IG':>8} {'z':>6} {'p':>7}   |  held-out CV: {'H_glob':>7} {'H_col':>7} {'Δ(gen)':>7}")
    for name,ix in FIELDS.items():
        pairs=[(c[ix],c[3]) for _,cl in rows for c in cl]
        h0,hc,ig,nmean,z,p=ig_with_null(pairs)
        Hg,Hc,gen=heldout(rows,ix)
        flag = '  <==' if (name=='core' and p<0.01 and gen>0.05) else ''
        print(f"  {name:7s} {h0:6.2f} {hc:9.2f} {ig:6.3f} {nmean:8.3f} {z:6.1f} {p:7.4f}   |              {Hg:7.2f} {Hc:7.2f} {gen:+7.3f}{flag}")
    # closure headline: distinct cores per column
    bycol=defaultdict(set); tot=set()
    for _,cl in rows:
        for c in cl: bycol[c[3]].add(c[1]); tot.add(c[1])
    order=['p0','p1','p2','p3','p4','mid','last']
    print(f"  open-key closure (distinct CORE values): global={len(tot)} | " +
          " ".join(f"{k}:{len(bycol[k])}" for k in order if k in bycol))
    print()

print("READ: a real Contact-style closure = CORE shows p<0.01 vs shuffle AND a")
print("positive held-out Δ(gen) that is LARGE relative to prefix/suffix (the template")
print("floor). If core's Δ(gen) merely tracks the closed enums, the column axis is")
print("just re-expressing known positional template structure — another content-free null.")

**In-sample, the column axis looks electric.** Conditioning the open-key core on column position cuts its entropy by 0.43–0.75 bits and beats the shuffle null at **z = 17–40, p ≈ 0.003** (the permutation floor) in every stratum. If I stopped here I'd be announcing a crack.

The closure headline says the same thing directly: in recipes/B, fixing the column leaves 359–511 of the 1,146 distinct cores in play. **The open key does not close.**

**And the discriminator kills the semantic reading outright.** The whole point of running prefix/suffix through the identical pipeline was to measure the template floor. The core's generalizable column signal does **not exceed** it:

| stratum | core Δ(gen) | prefix Δ(gen) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| herbal/A | +0.031 | **+0.092** | core *below* the closed-enum floor |
| recipes/B | +0.062 | +0.078 | core ≤ floor |
| bio/B | +0.066 | +0.065 | core ≈ floor |
| herbal/B | +0.066 | +0.038 | core ≈ floor |

The column axis is re-expressing the positional *template* grammar `columns.py` already documented (first-word lengthening, q-prefix positional law) — not a hidden semantic field. The huge in-sample IG is the same mirage K1/K11 warned about: structure that a content-free positional template reproduces. **Another null reproduced.** Rotating the substrate found the registration mark and turned it — and behind it was the template, not a message.

The §5 filter did exactly its job: the z=40 in-sample number is what every dead literature "solution" reports; the held-out collapse is why they're dead.

## Done

The Hadden move was the right instinct and I'm glad we made it — D2 genuinely reads like a registration mark, and the only way to know was to turn it. It turned. Behind it was the template, not a message.

**What happened:** `contact.py` rotated the corpus onto the column axis (word-index-within-line) and asked whether the open semantic key (D3's stubborn 6.8-bit core) closes. In-sample it *screams* yes — z = 17–40 against a shuffle null in all four strata. Out-of-sample it's ~1% of the key's entropy and doesn't beat the prefix/suffix template floor. Logged as **K12**.

The lasting takeaway is sharper than the result itself: **K12 is a calibration of what a false positive looks like here.** A z=40 in-sample number — exactly what the literature's "I cracked it" papers report — survived to one decimal place and then died on the held-out split. That in-sample/electric → held-out/collapse gap is now the project's diagnostic signature, and it's written into both the ledger and memory.

**Why this differs from Contact, restated:** Hadden's reveal was guaranteed to pay off because the primer was *built to be decoded*. Our every rotation just hands the content-free template another axis to reproduce. The asemic verdict isn't "we failed to find the dimension" — it's "the artifact has no dimension that closes," and K1/K10/K11/K12 are four independent rotations all returning the template.

**Ledger now carries** two genuinely *unrotated* axes, both cheap, both with weak priors:
- **L7 — quire/codicology order.** The most literal Contact analog left: every position confound (confound #2) used the *rebound* shelf order, not production order. Re-running on Fagin Davis's reconstructed gatherings could dissolve or sharpen half our nulls. Needs the quire-reconstruction mapping.
- **L8 — row axis.** The other half of "stack the pages" — line-as-record with columns aligned across rows. Weak after K12 but untested.

R1 (crib-anchored held-out decode) remains the only test that could *overturn* the verdict rather than re-confirm it. If you want to keep going, my order would be **L7 first** (it can undermine a confound we lean on everywhere, so it's high-leverage regardless of outcome), then R1 as the last genuine swing at meaning.

"""
L7 — CODICOLOGY RE-RUN: is confound #2's vocabulary autocorrelation a smooth
READING-ORDER (shelf-position) decay, or a step-function at PRODUCTION units
(quire / scribal hand — leaves written together)?

Why it matters: every control for confound #2 partials out *folio distance in
current binding order*. If the real driver is "same gathering / same scribe," then
(a) signals that "survived" a distance control but actually track quire identity are
weaker than credited, and (b) the correct thing to partial out is quire+hand.

Design: section/quire/reading-distance are mutually confounded (book laid out by
topic in order), so the decisive run is WITHIN ONE SECTION that spans multiple
quires, hands, and both Currier dialects — the herbal. There, topic is held
constant and we can ask what's left driving folio-to-folio vocabulary similarity.

Metric: per-folio L2-normalized CORE-frequency vector (the content field, D3);
pairwise cosine similarity; OLS of similarity on standardized predictors.
Caveat: this tests quire-as-production-unit + scribe, NOT Fagin Davis's specific
bifolio reordering (needs external data). It's the in-repo 80% of L7.
"""
import json, math, re
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict

PRE=['qok','qot','qo','ok','ot','o','y','ch','sh','d','cth','ckh','cph','cfh']
SUF=['eedy','eody','edy','aiin','aiir','ain','iin','dy','ol','or','ar','al','am','dam','ey','eey','y']
def core(w):
    p=next((x for x in sorted(PRE,key=len,reverse=True) if w.startswith(x)),'')
    r=w[len(p):]; s=next((x for x in sorted(SUF,key=len,reverse=True) if r.endswith(x) and len(r)>len(x)),'')
    return r[:len(r)-len(s)] if s else r

d=json.load(open('body_spatial.json'))
toks=d['tokens']

# folio reading order
order=OrderedDict()
for t in toks: order.setdefault(t['folio'],len(order))

def folio_vectors(section=None):
    vec=defaultdict(Counter); meta={}
    for t in toks:
        if section and t['section']!=section: continue
        if t.get('role')!='paragraph' or t['uncertain'] or '?' in t['word'] or len(t['word'])<2: continue
        f=t['folio']; vec[f][core(t['word'])]+=1
        meta[f]=(t['quire'],t['hand'],t['currier'])
    return vec,meta

def cosine(a,b):
    keys=set(a)|set(b);
    dot=sum(a[k]*b[k] for k in keys)
    na=math.sqrt(sum(v*v for v in a.values())); nb=math.sqrt(sum(v*v for v in b.values()))
    return dot/(na*nb) if na and nb else 0.0

def ols(X,y):
    """return betas, R2 with intercept; X columns already include intercept."""
    beta,_,_,_=np.linalg.lstsq(X,y,rcond=None)
    yhat=X@beta; ss_res=((y-yhat)**2).sum(); ss_tot=((y-y.mean())**2).sum()
    return beta,1-ss_res/ss_tot

def run(label, section):
    vec,meta=folio_vectors(section)
    fols=[f for f in vec if sum(vec[f].values())>=80]
    fols.sort(key=lambda f:order[f])
    print("="*78); print(f"{label}: {len(fols)} folios "
          f"(quires={len(set(meta[f][0] for f in fols))}, "
          f"hands={sorted(set(meta[f][1] for f in fols))}, "
          f"currier={sorted(set(meta[f][2] for f in fols))})"); print("="*78)
    if len(fols)<12: print("  too few folios\n"); return
    rows=[]
    for i in range(len(fols)):
        for j in range(i+1,len(fols)):
            fi,fj=fols[i],fols[j]
            qi,hi,ci=meta[fi]; qj,hj,cj=meta[fj]
            rd=abs(order[fi]-order[fj])
            rows.append((cosine(vec[fi],vec[fj]), rd,
                         1.0 if qi==qj else 0.0,
                         1.0 if (hi==hj and hi!='?') else 0.0,
                         1.0 if ci==cj else 0.0))
    A=np.array(rows); y=A[:,0]
    rd=A[:,1]; sq=A[:,2]; sh=A[:,3]; sc=A[:,4]
    def z(x): return (x-x.mean())/(x.std()+1e-12)
    # raw correlations
    print(f"  raw corr(similarity, predictor):")
    print(f"    reading-distance {np.corrcoef(y,rd)[0,1]:+.3f} | same-quire {np.corrcoef(y,sq)[0,1]:+.3f} "
          f"| same-hand {np.corrcoef(y,sh)[0,1]:+.3f} | same-currier {np.corrcoef(y,sc)[0,1]:+.3f}")
    # full model, standardized

## Result: confound #2 is block-structured, not a smooth decay — a useful sharpening, not a crack

The decisive run is the herbal (the only section with real variation across quire, hand, *and* both Currier dialects — topic held constant). Reading it straight:

| predictor | raw corr w/ folio-similarity | net effect (OLS) |
|---|---|---|
| same-Currier | **+0.518** | **+0.136** (dominates) |
| same-hand | +0.453 | +0.019 |
| same-quire | +0.120 | +0.032 |
| reading-distance | −0.099 | **−0.002 (~0)** |

And the clincher: **partial corr(reading-distance \| quire, hand, currier) = −0.012.** The smooth "shelf-position decay" that confound #2 has us partialling out **is essentially zero once you control for production/dialect blocks.** What looked like a distance gradient was block membership all along. There's also a real, smaller quire-boundary *step*: at matched short reading distance (≤8 leaves), same-quire pairs sit at 0.600 vs 0.541 across a boundary (Δ=+0.059) — a discontinuity a distance-only control can't see.

(The other sections are single-quire/single-hand/single-Currier, so they degenerate to `nan` — can't separate the predictors there. Expected; the herbal was always the test.)

**What this is and isn't:**
- It is *not* the dramatic Hadden payoff (the hoped-for "production order differs from shelf order and everything shifts"). The opposite, really: because the unit is the **quire/dialect block**, not fine reading position, Fagin Davis's bifolio *reordering* wouldn't move much.
- It *is* a real methodological correction. Confound #2 should be modeled as **discrete block membership (Currier ≫ quire ≈ hand), not a smooth folio-distance term.** A distance-only control under-corrects within-quire pairs and over-corrects across boundaries — it was leaky. Every future test should partial out quire+hand+Currier, not distance.
- It does *not* resurrect any killed claim (those died to stronger controls) and creates no meaning. Currier dominating just re-confirms confound #1 is the giant.

Logging it as a refinement to the confound catalog rather than a kill or a meaning finding.

Both substrate rotations are now done, and they point the same way:

So the honest verdict on the Hadden question: **we made the move, twice, and there is no hidden third dimension in the geometry of the substrate.** That's not a failure of imagination — it's the asemic hypothesis surviving two more falsification attempts. The difference from *Contact* holds: Ellie's primer was *built to reward* the rotation; this artifact rewards every rotation with the template that generated it.

My recommendation: **run R1.** It's the only remaining test whose *positive* outcome would matter, and it sidesteps the dimensional dead-end entirely. Want me to build it?
